cards.text: Moses is all grown up now. One day he goes out to his own people, the Hebrews, and watches their hard labor. Then he sees something that stops him in his tracks.

cards.question: While watching the Hebrews at their hard labor, Moses sees an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his own people.

cards.text: Moses looks this way. Then he looks that way, and he sees no one.

cards.question: With nobody around, what does Moses do to the Egyptian who was beating the Hebrew?
Moses hides the Egyptian's body in the ___.

cards.text: The next day Moses goes out again. This time it's two Hebrews fighting each other.

cards.question: Moses steps into the fight between the two Hebrews. Which one does he question?

cards.text: Moses asks him, "Why are you attacking your companion?" And the man fires right back, "Who made you ruler and judge over us?"

cards.question: The Hebrew man isn't done with Moses yet. What does he bring up next?

answers.text: The palace Moses grew up in

cards.text: Moses is afraid and thinks, "This thing I have done has surely become known." That's the face you make one second after you hit REPLY ALL.

cards.question: When Pharaoh, king of Egypt, hears about what Moses did, he lets it slide.

cards.text: Pharaoh wants Moses dead. So Moses does what anybody would do, friend. He RUNS.

cards.question: Moses flees from Pharaoh and settles in the land of ___.

cards.text: There in Midian, Moses sits down beside a well. Long way from the palace, and I bet that seat felt GOOD.
Now the priest of Midian has seven daughters. They come to that well to draw water and fill the troughs for their father's flock.

cards.question: Some shepherds come along and drive the daughters away. This time Moses stays seated and stays out of it.
Moses rose up to help the daughters and ___ their flock.

cards.text: The daughters head home to their father Reuel, the priest of Midian. He takes one look at them and has a question.

cards.question: What surprises Reuel when his seven daughters walk in?
The daughters tell Reuel that a Hebrew rescued them from the shepherds.

cards.text: "An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds," they tell him. The man ran all the way OUT of Egypt and STILL got called an Egyptian.
Reuel asks, "So where is he?" and then, "Why did you leave the man behind?" This man saves your whole morning and you LEFT him at the WELL?

cards.question: Reuel wants to do something for the man who helped his daughters. What does he tell them?

answers.text: Invite him to have something to eat
Pay him for watering the flock
Send him safely back to Egypt

cards.text: Moses agrees to stay with Reuel. And friend, this visit turns into a whole lot more than a visit.

cards.question: Reuel gives Moses one of his daughters in marriage. What is her name?
Zipporah gives birth to a son, and Moses names him Gershom. Moses says he has become a ___ in a foreign land.

cards.text: After a long time, the king of Egypt dies. The Israelites groan and cry out under their burden of slavery.

cards.question: The Israelites cry out for deliverance from their bondage. Where does their cry go?
God heard their groaning, and He remembered His ___ with Abraham, Isaac, and ___.
God sees the Israelites, but He doesn't take notice of them.

cards.text: That's where we pull this batch out for today, friend. But keep your apron ON, because this story is just warming up.

findings.problem: The passage picks up mid-story (passage 3 of the group, 'after Moses had grown up'), but the opening card gives no context on who Moses is: a Hebrew raised as the son of Pharaoh's daughter (Exodus 2:10). Later cards lean on that background. Card 9's wrong answer mentions 'the palace Moses grew up in', card 14 says 'Long way from the palace', and stop 2 card 7's joke is about Moses being called an Egyptian. None of these land without the setup.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: 'Long way from the palace' brings in a fact from outside the passage (Moses' upbringing, Exodus 2:10). The passage never mentions a palace, the card cites only Exodus 2:15, and no earlier card in this lesson sets up the palace.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'What surprises Reuel' states a feeling as fact. The text only says he asks why they returned so early (Exodus 2:18). It never says he was surprised.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse, but it cites Exodus 2:25, which card 16 already asks. The docs allow this card to be only the line, but they don't say what it should cite.
findings.question: When the final story card is only the 'story isn't over' line, what should its verses field cite: the passage's last verse, nothing, or something else?
